results.evidence: Retry: a trail guide measures the Snowgrass Trail at 1.9 mi to the Goat Creek bridge, 4.7 mi to the Lily Basin junction and 5.4 mi to the PCT junction, with Old Snowy a further ~1.8 mi north on the PCT plus ~0.5 mi; two independent trip reports put the whole two-summit outing at about 14 mi (14.2 mi; 'about 14 miles') and one camped at ~7,200 ft west of Peak 7771. That makes day 1 (camp beyond the PCT junction) roughly 6-6.5 mi rather than 7, but no source states the trailhead-to-camp mileage, and the PCT-junction pin (5 vs 5.4) is a single-source difference. Would settle it: a GPS track or report stating the distance from the trailhead to a ~7,200 ft camp.

Retry: one party did the whole Old Snowy + Ives trip car-to-car in 8 hours (fast, single day); another took 7.3 h for the Old Snowy/Ives loop from a lower camp alone. Neither states the length of a camp-to-summits-to-trailhead day, so neither the 8 h figure nor the 5:30 AM-to-5 PM schedule can be confirmed by two sources. Would settle it: a report timing the summit loop plus hike-out from a high camp.

Retry: one 2011 report gives about 3,700 ft of gain car-to-car for the Old Snowy + Ives outing, and a route summary gives roughly 3,600 ft for the ~14 mi round trip; both exceed gain_ft 3,400 but they do not agree on one figure, and changing day 2's 900 ft would break the itinerary total unless gain_ft also changes. Would settle it: a second source stating the same car-to-car gain (e.g. two GPS-tracked reports).

A Northwest Face trip report states 2,425 ft of gain from the hairpin; a GPS-tracked report on the same hairpin-to-summit approach (North Face, same summit and trailhead) logged 754 m (~2,474 ft); the row's own trailhead (5,160) and summit (7,572) differ by ~2,412 ft. gain_ft 1,900 is below even the net rise; 2,425 is the figure stated for this route and agrees with loss_ft 2,500.

patches.expect:
NEVER CROSS KANGAROO PASS. THAT IS THE NEGATIVE TEST AND IT IS ABSOLUTE: THE NORTH AND NORTHWEST FACE ROUTES BOTH GO OVER THE PASS AND THEN TRAVERSE BENEATH WALLABY'S SLABS. THIS ONE DOES NOT GO THERE AT ALL. IF YOU ARE STANDING IN A BROAD, VIEW-FILLED SADDLE, YOU HAVE TAKEN THE WRONG APPROACH.

THE POSITIVE INSTRUCTION IS A SIDE-OF-THE-CREEK TEST, WHICH IS EXACTLY THE KIND THAT SURVIVES FOG: HIKE SOUTHEAST ON THE RIGHT SIDE OF THE CREEK. Water on your left the whole way up. The trail IMPROVES past several slide and boulder areas, which is the opposite of what the Kangaroo Pass path does, so the tread itself tells you which line you are on.

AND THE FACT THAT SHOULD SHAPE THE WHOLE PLAN, BECAUSE IT REMOVES THE OBVIOUS METHOD OF CONFIRMING YOUR OBJECTIVE: THE SOUTH FACE IS NOT VISIBLE FROM THE HIGHWAY. You cannot look at it from the car and pick your line, which is how most parties orient themselves at Washington Pass. Commit to the creek-side approach and read the wall when you arrive under it.

EXPECT IT TO BE LONGER AND STEEPER than the north-side approach. If your walk is taking about an hour to a pass, you are on the wrong one.
patches.value:
THE SOUTH FACE SHARES THE KANGAROO PASS APPROACH AND SPLITS FROM THE OTHER ROUTES ONLY BEYOND THE PASS.

From the hairpin, follow the climbers' trail through the boulder fields and forest up to Kangaroo Pass, about an hour. The North and Northwest Face routes then traverse to the gully below the notch between the Temple and Little Finger and go UP it. THIS ROUTE DOES NOT CLIMB TOWARD THE NOTCH: drop some height below the pass and traverse across to the base of the South Face, on the far side of the formation.

SO THE NEGATIVE TEST IS: IF YOU ARE ASCENDING THE GULLY TOWARD THE NOTCH, YOU ARE ON THE WAY TO THE NORTH-SIDE ROUTES, NOT THIS ONE.

THE SOUTH FACE IS NOT VISIBLE FROM THE HIGHWAY, so you cannot pick your line from the car; read the wall when you arrive under it. Expect the walk to the base to take roughly 2.5 to 4 hours, longer than the approach to the north-side routes.

Returning to the base after the climb is awkward, so carry everything up the route with you; poles can be left at the pass and collected on the way out.
patches.fact: Route identity (South Face vs Southwest Face)
